task: terminate two Cat5e runs into keystone jacks (smoke fixture)
note: Hand-written plan override, not Planner output. The real Planner writes close-up evidence lines (e.g. a photo of the T568B label on the jack); these 6 archive photos were wide shots taken months earlier for another purpose, so nothing satisfies a Planner-written step. Evidence lines below are written to match exactly what these photos DO show, the same approach as data/demo/onq-keystone/e2e3.py.

steps.title: Confirm the low-voltage panel
steps.action: Open the structured-wiring panel and check you see only coax and Cat5e cable runs, a splitter and a telecom module, not any circuit breakers.
do_not_touch: the coax splitter's connected cable ends
steps.stop_condition: if any breaker or orange/red mains wire is visible in the box, stop and get a licensed electrician
steps.evidence_required: the open low-voltage panel box in one wide frame, showing the coax splitter and telecom module with cable runs, and no circuit breakers anywhere in the photo

steps.title: Seat the wire pairs into the office jack
steps.action: At the office wall box, hold the keystone jack (the small snap-in socket the cable plugs into) out with its faceplate off, and lay the loose coloured wire pairs from the cable against the jack body before punching them down.
do_not_touch: the blue cable already looped into the wall box
steps.evidence_required: the wall box open with the faceplate off, the keystone jack held out (not yet snapped into the plate), and the coloured wire pairs visibly laid against or into the jack body

steps.title: Confirm the run lands at the telecom module
steps.action: At the panel, confirm the Cat5e run for the office jack is punched down into one of the telecom module's numbered ports.
steps.evidence_required: a close-up of the telecom module showing wire pairs punched into at least one numbered port block, with the port labels legible
